entries.name: arch.unitroot.unitroot.mackinnoncrit
entries.summary: Return the critical values for cointegrating and the ADF test.
keywords: Return the critical values for cointegrating and the ADF test. The critical values are from response surface regressions that follow the methodology of MacKinnon (2010), and depend on the number of observations. Parameters ---------- num_unit_roots : int, optional The number of series of I(1) series for which the null of non-cointegration is being tested, from 1 to 12. For the ADF test, N = 1. Values larger than 1 are only available when `dist_type` is "adf-t" and `regression` is not "n". regression : {"c", "ct", "ctt", "n"}, optional Following MacKinnon (1996), these stand for the type of regression run. "c" for constant and no trend, "ct" for constant with a linear trend, "ctt" for constant with a linear and quadratic trend, and "n" for no constant. Not case sensitive. nobs : int or float, optional This is the sample size, the number of observations in the regression of the test, which must be positive. If the sample size is numpy.inf, then the asymptotic critical values are returned. dist_type : {"adf-t", "adf-z", "dfgls"}, optional Type of test statistic. Not case sensitive. Returns ------- crit_vals : ndarray Three critical values corresponding to 1%, 5% and 10% cut-offs. Raises ------ TypeError If `num_unit_roots` is not an integer, `nobs` is not a real number or `regression` or `dist_type` is not a str. ValueError If `num_unit_roots` is not between 1 and 12 (1 if `regression` is "n"), `nobs` is not positive or is NaN, `regression` or `dist_type` is not one of the options, or `num_unit_roots` is larger than 1 when `dist_type` is not "adf-t". Notes ----- The values for the ADF t-test with one unit root and for the ADF z-test are fit to the same simulations as the p-values of mackinnonp, and the p-values of the asymptotic critical values are 1%, 5% and 10%. The values for the DFGLS test are also fit to new simulations. The values for the ADF t-test with more than one unit root are from MacKinnon (2010). References ---------- MacKinnon, J.G. 1994 "Approximate Asymptotic Distribution Functions for Unit-Root and Cointegration Tests." Journal of Business & Economics Statistics, 12.2, 167-76. MacKinnon, J.G. 2010. "Critical Values for Cointegration Tests." Queen's University, Dept of Economics Working Papers 1227. https://ideas.repec.org/p/qed/wpaper/1227.html

entries.name: arch.unitroot.unitroot.mackinnonp
entries.summary: Return MacKinnon's approximate p-value for test stat.
keywords: Return MacKinnon's approximate p-value for test stat. Parameters ---------- stat : float "T-value" from an Augmented Dickey-Fuller or DFGLS regression. It can be inf or -inf, but not NaN. regression : {"c", "n", "ct", "ctt"}, optional This is the method of regression that was used. Following MacKinnon's notation, this can be "c" for constant, "n" for no constant, "ct" for constant and trend, and "ctt" for constant, trend, and trend-squared. Not case sensitive. num_unit_roots : int, optional The number of series believed to be I(1), from 1 to 6. For (Augmented) Dickey-Fuller N = 1. Values larger than 1 are only available when `dist_type` is "adf-t". dist_type : {"adf-t", "adf-z", "dfgls"}, optional The test type to use when computing p-values. Not case sensitive. Options include - "adf-t" - ADF t-stat based test - "adf-z" - ADF z test - "dfgls" - GLS detrended Dickey Fuller Returns ------- p-value : float The approximate asymptotic p-value of the statistic. Raises ------ TypeError If `stat` is not a real number, `num_unit_roots` is not an integer or `regression` or `dist_type` is not a str. ValueError If `stat` is NaN, `num_unit_roots` is not between 1 and 6, `regression` or `dist_type` is not one of the options, or `num_unit_roots` is larger than 1 when `dist_type` is not "adf-t". Notes ----- The values for the ADF t-test with one unit root, the ADF z-test and the DFGLS test are fit to new simulations following the methodology of MacKinnon (1994), and are smooth and increasing functions of the statistic. The values for the ADF t-test with more than one unit root are from MacKinnon (1994). References ---------- MacKinnon, J.G. 1994 "Approximate Asymptotic Distribution Functions for Unit-Root and Cointegration Tests." Journal of Business & Economics Statistics, 12.2, 167-76.

entries.name: arch.univariate.APARCH
entries.summary: Asymmetric Power ARCH (APARCH) volatility process.
keywords: Asymmetric Power ARCH (APARCH) volatility process. Parameters ---------- p : int, optional Order of the symmetric innovation. Must satisfy p>=o and be positive. o : int, optional Order of the asymmetric innovation. Must satisfy o<=p and be non-negative. q : int, optional Order of the lagged (transformed) conditional variance. Must be non-negative. delta : float, optional Value to use for a fixed delta in the APARCH model. If not provided, the value of delta is jointly estimated with other model parameters. User provided delta is restricted to lie in (0.05, 4.0). common_asym : bool, optional Restrict all asymmetry terms to share the same asymmetry parameter. If False (default), then there are no restrictions on the ``o`` asymmetry parameters. Raises ------ TypeError If ``p``, ``o`` or ``q`` is not an integer, ``delta`` is not a real number or None, or ``common_asym`` is not a bool. ValueError If ``p`` is smaller than 1, ``o`` or ``q`` is negative, ``o`` is larger than ``p``, or ``delta`` is NaN, inf or not in (0.05, 4.0). Notes ----- In this class of processes, the variance dynamics are .. math:: \sigma_{t}^{\delta}=\omega +\sum_{i=1}^{p}\alpha_{i} \left(\left|\epsilon_{t-i}\right| -\gamma_{i}I_{[o\geq i]}\epsilon_{t-i}\right)^{\delta} +\sum_{k=1}^{q}\beta_{k}\sigma_{t-k}^{\delta} If ``common_asym`` is ``True``, then all of :math:`\gamma_i` are restricted to have a common value.

entries.name: arch.univariate.ARCHInMean
entries.summary: (G)ARCH-in-mean model and simulation.
keywords: (G)ARCH-in-mean model and simulation. Parameters ---------- y : array_like or Series, optional Vector of nobs elements containing the dependent variable. x : array_like or DataFrame, optional Array with nobs rows and k columns containing exogenous regressors. Must contain only finite values. lags : int or array_like, optional Description of lag structure of the AR. Scalar included all lags between 1 and the value. A 1-d array includes the AR lags lags[0], lags[1], ... The lags must be integers (2.5, 5.0 and True are not accepted). A scalar must be at least 0, and the values of an array at least 1. constant : bool, optional Flag whether the model should include a constant. hold_back : int, optional Number of observations at the start of the sample to exclude when estimating model parameters. Used when comparing models with different lag lengths to estimate on the common sample. Must be a non-negative integer. volatility : VolatilityProcess, optional Volatility process to use in the model. ``volatility.updateable`` must return ``True``. distribution : Distribution, optional Error distribution to use in the model. rescale : bool, optional Flag indicating whether to automatically rescale data if the scale of the data is likely to produce convergence issues when estimating model parameters. If False, the model is estimated on the data without transformation. If True, then y is rescaled and the new scale is reported in the estimation results. If None, the data is not rescaled and a warning is issued when its scale is likely to produce convergence issues. form : {"log", "vol", "var"}, int or float, optional The form of the conditional variance that appears in the mean equation. The string names use the log of the conditional variance ("log"), the square-root of the conditional variance ("vol") or the conditional variance. When specified using a float, interpreted as :math:`\sigma_t^{form}` so that 1 is equivalent to "vol" and 2 is equivalent to "var". When using a number, must be finite and different from 0. The strings are not case sensitive. Raises ------ TypeError If ``lags`` or ``hold_back`` is not an integer (a float, including 5.0, and a bool are not accepted), if ``constant`` or ``rescale`` is not a bool (``rescale`` can also be None), if ``volatility`` or ``distribution`` is not an instance of :class:`~arch.univariate.volatility.VolatilityProcess` or :class:`~arch.univariate.distribution.Distribution`, or if ``x`` cannot be converted to numbers, or if ``form`` is not a string or a number. ValueError If ``lags`` is negative, empty or in an unsupported format, if the largest lag is not smaller than the number of observations, if ``hold_back`` is negative, if ``form`` is a string other than "log", "vol" or "var" or is not finite or is 0, or if ``x`` contains NaN or inf or does not have a row for each observation of ``y``. Notes ----- The (G)arch-in-mean model with exogenous regressors (-X) is described by .. math:: y_t = \mu + \kappa f(\sigma^2_t)+ \sum_{i=1}^p \phi_{L_{i}} y_{t-L_{i}} + \gamma' x_t + \epsilon_t where :math:`f(\cdot)` is the function specified by ``form``.

entries.name: arch.univariate.FIAPARCH
entries.summary: Fractionally Integrated Asymmetric Power ARCH (FIAPARCH) volatility process.
keywords: Fractionally Integrated Asymmetric Power ARCH (FIAPARCH) volatility process. Parameters ---------- p : {0, 1}, optional Order of the symmetric innovation. o : {0, 1}, optional Order of the asymmetric innovation. q : {0, 1}, optional Order of the lagged (transformed) conditional variance. delta : float, optional Value to use for a fixed delta in the model. If not provided, the value of delta is jointly estimated with other model parameters. User provided delta is restricted to lie in (0.05, 4.0). truncation : int, optional Truncation point to use in ARCH(:math:`\infty`) representation. Default is 1000. Must be positive. Raises ------ TypeError If ``p``, ``o``, ``q`` or ``truncation`` is not an integer, or ``delta`` is not a real number or None. ValueError If ``p``, ``o`` or ``q`` is not 0 or 1, ``truncation`` is smaller than 1, or ``delta`` is NaN, inf or not in (0.05, 4.0). Notes ----- In this class of processes, the variance dynamics are .. math:: \sigma_t^{\delta} = \omega + [1-\beta L - (1-\phi L)(1-L)^d] (|\epsilon_{t}| - \gamma \epsilon_{t})^{\delta} + \beta \sigma_{t-1}^{\delta} where ``L`` is the lag operator, ``d`` is the fractional differencing parameter, and ``gamma`` controls asymmetry. The model is estimated using the ARCH(:math:`\infty`) representation, .. math:: \sigma_t^{\delta} = (1-\beta)^{-1} \omega + \sum_{i=1}^{\infty} \lambda_i (|\epsilon_{t-i}| - \gamma \epsilon_{t-i})^{\delta} The weights :math:`\lambda_i` are identical to those used in FIGARCH.

entries.summary: FIGARCH model.
keywords: FIGARCH model. Parameters ---------- p : {0, 1}, optional Order of the symmetric innovation. q : {0, 1}, optional Order of the lagged (transformed) conditional variance. power : float, optional Power to use with the innovations, abs(e) ** power. Default is 2.0, which produces FIGARCH and related models. Using 1.0 produces FIAVARCH and related models. Other powers can be specified, although these should be strictly positive, and usually larger than 0.25. truncation : int, optional Truncation point to use in ARCH(:math:`\infty`) representation. Notes ----- In this class of processes, the variance dynamics are .. math:: h_t = \omega + [1-\beta L - (1-\phi L) (1-L)^d] \epsilon_t^2 + \beta h_{t-1} where ``L`` is the lag operator and ``d`` is the fractional differencing parameter. The model is estimated using the ARCH(:math:`\infty`) representation, .. math:: h_t = (1-\beta)^{-1} \omega + \sum_{i=1}^\infty \lambda_i \epsilon_{t-i}^2 The weights are constructed using .. math:: \delta_1 = d \\ \lambda_1 = d - \beta + \phi and the recursive equations .. math:: \delta_j = \frac{j - 1 - d}{j} \delta_{j-1} \\ \lambda_j = \beta \lambda_{j-1} + \delta_j - \phi \delta_{j-1}. When `power` is not 2, the ARCH(:math:`\infty`) representation is still used where :math:`\epsilon_t^2` is replaced by :math:`|\epsilon_t|^p` and ``p`` is the power.

entries.name: arch.univariate.MAMean
entries.summary: Moving average (MA) mean model, with optional constant.
keywords: Moving average (MA) mean model, with optional constant. Provides model estimation, simulation and forecasting. Parameters ---------- y : array_like or Series, optional Vector of nobs elements containing the dependent variable. lags : int, optional The order of the moving average, q. Must be at least 1. constant : bool, optional Flag whether the model should include a constant. hold_back : int, optional Number of observations at the start of the sample to exclude when estimating model parameters. Must be a non-negative integer. volatility : VolatilityProcess, optional Volatility process to use in the model. distribution : Distribution, optional Error distribution to use in the model. rescale : bool, optional Flag indicating whether to automatically rescale data if the scale of the data is likely to produce convergence issues when estimating model parameters. If False, the model is estimated on the data without transformation. If True, then y is rescaled and the new scale is reported in the estimation results. If None, the data is not rescaled and a warning is issued when its scale is likely to produce convergence issues. Attributes ---------- lags : int The order of the moving average constant : bool Whether the model includes a constant Raises ------ TypeError If ``lags`` or ``hold_back`` is not an integer (a float, including 5.0, and a bool are not accepted), if ``constant`` or ``rescale`` is not a bool (``rescale`` can also be None), or if ``volatility`` or ``distribution`` is not an instance of :class:`~arch.univariate.volatility.VolatilityProcess` or :class:`~arch.univariate.distribution.Distribution`. ValueError If ``lags`` is smaller than 1 or ``hold_back`` is negative. Notes ----- The MA(q) model is .. math:: y_t = \mu + \epsilon_t + \theta_1 \epsilon_{t-1} + \ldots + \theta_q \epsilon_{t-q} where the innovations :math:`\epsilon_t=\sigma_t e_t` have the conditional variance :math:`\sigma^2_t` of the volatility process and :math:`e_t` has the distribution of the model. The parameters are ordered :math:`[\mu, \theta_1, \ldots, \theta_q]`, and :math:`\mu` is not included when ``constant`` is False. The innovations are not observed. They are computed recursively using .. math:: \epsilon_t = y_t - \mu - \theta_1 \epsilon_{t-1} - \ldots - \theta_q \epsilon_{t-q} where the innovations before the first observation in the estimation sample are 0. This is the conditional likelihood, and its effect vanishes when the process is invertible, that is when all roots of :math:`1+\theta_1 z+\ldots+\theta_q z^q` are outside of the unit circle. Starting values are invertible. Invertibility is imposed when q is 1 or 2 (by bounds and linear constraints, respectively), but is not imposed for larger q since the restrictions are nonlinear. The sample used to estimate the parameters is also the sample used to compute the innovations, and so observations excluded using ``hold_back`` or when fitting are not used. The mean forecast of :math:`y_{T+h}` is :math:`\mu + \sum_{j=h}^{q}\theta_j\epsilon_{T+h-j}`, which uses the last :math:`q-h+1` innovations if :math:`h \leq q`, and is :math:`\mu` after that. The forecast variance is :math:`\sum_{j=0}^{h-1}\psi_j^2\sigma^2_{T+h-j}` with :math:`\psi_0=1`, :math:`\psi_j=\theta_j` for :math:`j\leq q` and 0 otherwise. Exogenous regressors are not supported.

entries.name: arch.univariate.NGARCH
entries.summary: Nonlinear asymmetric GARCH (NGARCH) volatility process.
keywords: Nonlinear asymmetric GARCH (NGARCH) volatility process. The process of Engle and Ng [1]_, which is called NAGARCH in the rugarch package for R. Parameters ---------- p : int, optional Order of the symmetric innovation. Must satisfy p>=o and be positive. o : int, optional Number of innovations that have a shift (an asymmetry parameter). Must satisfy o<=p and be non-negative. The first ``o`` of the ``p`` innovations are shifted. q : int, optional Order of the lagged conditional variance. Must be non-negative. Raises ------ TypeError If ``p``, ``o`` or ``q`` is not an integer. ValueError If ``p`` is smaller than 1, ``o`` or ``q`` is negative, or ``o`` is larger than ``p``. Notes ----- In this class of processes, the variance dynamics are .. math:: \sigma_{t}^{2}=\omega +\sum_{i=1}^{p}\alpha_{i} \left(\epsilon_{t-i}-\theta_{i}I_{[o\geq i]}\sigma_{t-i}\right)^{2} +\sum_{j=1}^{q}\beta_{j}\sigma_{t-j}^{2} which is :math:`\sigma_{t-i}^2 (e_{t-i}-\theta_{i})^2` in terms of the standardized shock :math:`e_{t}=\epsilon_{t}/\sigma_{t}`. The parameters are named ``omega``, ``alpha[i]``, ``theta[i]`` and ``beta[j]``. The shift :math:`\theta` is the position of the minimum of the news impact curve in units of the lagged volatility. The sign convention is that of the rugarch package and of most textbooks: a positive :math:`\theta` is the leverage effect, since a negative shock then raises the variance more than a positive shock of the same size. Engle and Ng [1]_ write the shift as :math:`(\epsilon_{t-1}+\gamma\sigma_{t-1})^2` and expect :math:`\gamma<0`, so that :math:`\theta=-\gamma`. The name NGARCH is also used for the nonlinear ARCH model of Higgins and Bera [2]_, which is a different model and is not available here. The expected value of :math:`(e_{t}-\theta)^2` is :math:`1+\theta^2` for any standardized distribution, since :math:`e_t` has mean 0 and variance 1. The process is covariance stationary if the persistence .. math:: \phi=\sum_{i=1}^{p}\alpha_{i}\left(1+\theta_{i}^{2}\right) +\sum_{j=1}^{q}\beta_{j} is smaller than 1, and then the unconditional variance of :math:`\epsilon_t` is :math:`\omega/(1-\phi)`. Analytic forecasts are exact at every horizon. When :math:`p=q=1`, they satisfy :math:`f_h=\omega+\phi f_{h-1}`. Estimation uses the linear constraints :math:`\omega,\alpha_i,\beta_j\geq 0` and :math:`\sum\alpha_i+\sum\beta_j<1`, as for :class:`~arch.univariate.APARCH`, and bounds of -5 and 5 for :math:`\theta`. The stationarity condition :math:`\phi<1` is not imposed during estimation, since it is not linear in the parameters, and a model with :math:`\theta\neq 0` can be estimated with a persistence of 1 or more. ``fit`` then issues a ``ValueWarning``. With ``o=0`` there is no shift and the process is a GARCH process, so :class:`~arch.univariate.GARCH` should be used instead. A ``ValueWarning`` is issued in this case. Before the start of the sample, the variance and the squared residual are both replaced by the backcast of the variance, so that each shock term is :math:`\alpha_i(1+\theta_i^2)` times the backcast. References ---------- .. [1] Engle, R. F., & Ng, V. K. (1993). Measuring and testing the impact of news on volatility. *The Journal of Finance*, 48(5), 1749-1778. .. [2] Higgins, M. L., & Bera, A. K. (1992). A class of nonlinear ARCH models. *International Economic Review*, 33(1), 137-158.

entries.name: arch.univariate.christoffersen_conditional_coverage
entries.summary: Christoffersen test of the conditional coverage of VaR.
keywords: Christoffersen test of the conditional coverage of VaR. Parameters ---------- returns : array_like Realized returns, a 1-d array of finite numbers with at least 2 observations. var : array_like VaR forecasts as positive losses, a 1-d array of finite numbers. See `var_exceptions` for the sign convention and for how the inputs are aligned. p : float, optional The probability of an exception that the VaR is designed for, which is the size of the tail, in the interval (0, 0.5]. It is 0.05 for a 95% VaR and 0.01 for a 99% VaR. The default is 0.05, a 95% VaR. Returns ------- arch.utility.testing.WaldTestStatistic The likelihood-ratio statistic, which is asymptotically :math:`\chi^2_2` under the null that exceptions are independent and have probability ``p``, with its p-value. Raises ------ TypeError If ``returns`` or ``var`` cannot be converted to numbers, or ``p`` is not a real number. ValueError If ``returns`` or ``var`` is not valid, as in `var_exceptions`, there are fewer than 2 observations, or ``p`` is not in (0, 0.5]. See Also -------- kupiec_pof : Test of the proportion of exceptions. christoffersen_independence : Test of the independence of the exceptions. Notes ----- The statistic of Christoffersen (1998) [1]_ is the sum of the Kupiec statistic, computed with all the observations, and the independence statistic, :math:`LR_{cc}=LR_{uc}+LR_{ind}`. See `kupiec_pof` and `christoffersen_independence` for the statistics and for the handling of series with no exceptions or with only exceptions. References ---------- .. [1] Christoffersen, P. F. (1998). Evaluating interval forecasts. International Economic Review, 39(4), 841-862.

entries.name: arch.univariate.christoffersen_independence
entries.summary: Christoffersen test of the independence of the exceptions of VaR.
keywords: Christoffersen test of the independence of the exceptions of VaR. Parameters ---------- returns : array_like Realized returns, a 1-d array of finite numbers with at least 2 observations. var : array_like VaR forecasts as positive losses, a 1-d array of finite numbers. See `var_exceptions` for the sign convention and for how the inputs are aligned. Returns ------- arch.utility.testing.WaldTestStatistic The likelihood-ratio statistic, which is asymptotically :math:`\chi^2_1` under the null that exceptions are independent, with its p-value. Raises ------ TypeError If ``returns`` or ``var`` cannot be converted to numbers. ValueError If ``returns`` or ``var`` is not valid, as in `var_exceptions`, or there are fewer than 2 observations. See Also -------- kupiec_pof : Test of the proportion of exceptions. christoffersen_conditional_coverage : Joint test of coverage and independence. Notes ----- The null is that the probability of an exception does not depend on whether the previous day was an exception, against a first-order Markov chain. With :math:`n_{ij}` the number of days in state :math:`j` that follow a day in state :math:`i` (1 is an exception), :math:`\hat{\pi}_{i}=n_{i1}/(n_{i0}+n_{i1})` and :math:`\hat{\pi}=(n_{01}+n_{11})/\sum n_{ij}`, the statistic of Christoffersen (1998) [1]_ is .. math:: LR_{ind} = -2\ln\left[\frac{(1-\hat{\pi})^{n_{00}+n_{10}} \hat{\pi}^{n_{01}+n_{11}}} {(1-\hat{\pi}_0)^{n_{00}}\hat{\pi}_0^{n_{01}} (1-\hat{\pi}_1)^{n_{10}}\hat{\pi}_1^{n_{11}}}\right]. The first observation is conditioned on, so the :math:`T-1` transitions are used. A term :math:`0\ln 0` is 0. If no day follows a state, for example when there is no exception before the last day, :math:`\hat{\pi}_i` is not defined and does not enter the statistic. The statistic is 0 for a series with no exceptions or only exceptions. A probability that is 0, because no exception follows an exception (:math:`n_{11}=0`), is evaluated at the limit. References ---------- .. [1] Christoffersen, P. F. (1998). Evaluating interval forecasts. International Economic Review, 39(4), 841-862.

entries.name: arch.univariate.hill_estimator
entries.summary: Hill tail-index estimator of standardized residuals.
keywords: Hill tail-index estimator of standardized residuals. Parameters ---------- std_resid : array_like Standardized residuals. The estimator is computed from the largest absolute standardized residuals after removing non-finite observations, since the residuals of a fitted model are NaN outside the estimation sample. k : int, optional Number of upper order statistics to use. If not provided, uses ``int(sqrt(n))`` where ``n`` is the number of finite residuals. Must be at least 1 and less than the number of non-zero finite residuals. Returns ------- float Inverse Hill estimate of the tail index. Raises ------ TypeError If ``std_resid`` cannot be converted to numbers or ``k`` is not an integer. ValueError If ``std_resid`` is not 1-d, has fewer than two non-zero finite observations, or ``k`` is outside the allowed range. Notes ----- The estimator is .. math:: \hat{\nu} = \left(k^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^k \log X_{n-i+1:n} - \log X_{n-k:n}\right)^{-1} where ``X`` contains the positive absolute standardized residuals.

entries.name: arch.univariate.kupiec_pof
entries.summary: Kupiec proportion-of-failures test of the coverage of VaR.
keywords: Kupiec proportion-of-failures test of the coverage of VaR. Parameters ---------- returns : array_like Realized returns, a 1-d array of finite numbers. var : array_like VaR forecasts as positive losses, a 1-d array of finite numbers. See `var_exceptions` for the sign convention and for how the inputs are aligned. p : float, optional The probability of an exception that the VaR is designed for, which is the size of the tail, in the interval (0, 0.5]. It is 0.05 for a 95% VaR and 0.01 for a 99% VaR. The default is 0.05, a 95% VaR. Returns ------- arch.utility.testing.WaldTestStatistic The likelihood-ratio statistic, which is asymptotically :math:`\chi^2_1` under the null that the probability of an exception is ``p``, with its p-value. Raises ------ TypeError If ``returns`` or ``var`` cannot be converted to numbers, or ``p`` is not a real number. ValueError If ``returns`` or ``var`` is not valid, as in `var_exceptions`, or ``p`` is not in (0, 0.5]. See Also -------- christoffersen_independence : Test of the independence of the exceptions. christoffersen_conditional_coverage : Joint test of coverage and independence. traffic_light : The Basel zone of the number of exceptions. Notes ----- With :math:`x` exceptions in :math:`T` observations and :math:`\hat{\pi}=x/T`, the statistic of Kupiec (1995) [1]_ is .. math:: LR_{uc} = -2\ln\left[\frac{(1-p)^{T-x}p^x} {(1-\hat{\pi})^{T-x}\hat{\pi}^x}\right]. The test is two-sided, so too few exceptions reject as well as too many. The terms :math:`0\ln 0` of a series with no exception, or only exceptions, are 0, which is the limit of the likelihood, so that the statistic is :math:`-2T\ln(1-p)` and :math:`-2T\ln p`. References ---------- .. [1] Kupiec, P. H. (1995). Techniques for verifying the accuracy of risk measurement models. The Journal of Derivatives, 3(2), 73-84.

entries.name: arch.univariate.traffic_light
entries.summary: Basel traffic light zone of the exceptions of VaR.
keywords: Basel traffic light zone of the exceptions of VaR. Parameters ---------- returns : array_like Realized returns, a 1-d array of finite numbers with at least ``window`` observations. var : array_like VaR forecasts as positive losses, a 1-d array of finite numbers. See `var_exceptions` for the sign convention and for how the inputs are aligned. p : float, optional The probability of an exception that the VaR is designed for, which is the size of the tail, in the interval (0, 0.5]. It is 0.05 for a 95% VaR and 0.01 for a 99% VaR. The default is 0.01, the 99% VaR of the Basel framework. window : int, optional The number of the most recent observations that are counted. It must be positive and no larger than the number of observations. The default is 250, about one year of daily data. Returns ------- TrafficLightResult The zone, the number of exceptions in the window, the cumulative binomial probability of that number of exceptions or fewer, the probability of that number or more (the type 1 error), the number of observations in the window and ``p``. Raises ------ TypeError If ``returns`` or ``var`` cannot be converted to numbers, ``p`` is not a real number or ``window`` is not an integer. ValueError If ``returns`` or ``var`` is not valid, as in `var_exceptions`, ``p`` is not in (0, 0.5], ``window`` is not positive, or there are fewer than ``window`` observations. See Also -------- kupiec_pof : Test of the proportion of exceptions. Notes ----- The framework of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (1996) [1]_ counts the exceptions in the last 250 days. If the probability of an exception is ``p``, the number of exceptions has a binomial distribution, and the cumulative probability :math:`P(X\leq x)` of the observed number :math:`x` sets the zone. The zone is green if the probability is below 95%, yellow if it is at least 95% and below 99.99%, and red if it is at least 99.99%, since the framework says that the yellow and the red zone begin where the probability equals or exceeds 95% and 99.99%. For 250 observations and ``p=0.01``, green is 0 to 4 exceptions, yellow is 5 to 9 and red is 10 or more, which are the boundaries of Table 2 of the framework. The framework deduces the boundaries for other sample sizes from the binomial distribution in the same way, as this function does. ``type1_error`` is :math:`P(X\geq x)`, the probability that an accurate model has :math:`x` or more exceptions. The two probabilities add up to more than 1 by the probability of exactly :math:`x` exceptions. A series with no exception is always green. Its cumulative probability is the probability of the smallest number of exceptions, which is above 95% when ``window * p`` is small, but no exception is never a sign of understated risk. A series with fewer than ``window`` observations raises an error rather than being tested with the observations that there are, because the zones of the framework are defined for a sample of the specified size. Set ``window`` to the number of observations to test a shorter series. References ---------- .. [1] Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (1996). Supervisory framework for the use of "backtesting" in conjunction with the internal models approach to market risk capital requirements.

entries.name: arch.univariate.var_exceptions
entries.summary: Identify the exceptions of a VaR forecast.
keywords: Identify the exceptions of a VaR forecast. Parameters ---------- returns : array_like Realized returns, a 1-d array of finite numbers. var : array_like VaR forecasts, a 1-d array of finite numbers. VaR is a positive loss, so that a VaR of 2.5 forecasts that the return is below -2.5 with the probability that the VaR is designed for. If both ``returns`` and ``var`` are Series, they are aligned on the index and the observations that are in both are used, in the order of ``returns``. Otherwise, they must have the same length and are matched by position. Returns ------- {ndarray, Series} A bool array that is True where the return is an exception, that is where the loss exceeds the VaR, ``-returns > var``. It is a Series named ``"exception"`` if ``returns`` or ``var`` is a pandas object, with the index of the observations that are used: the index of ``returns`` if it is a pandas object, and otherwise the index of ``var``. Raises ------ TypeError If ``returns`` or ``var`` cannot be converted to numbers. ValueError If ``returns`` or ``var`` is not a 1-d array of finite numbers (NaN and inf raise), has no observations, has an index with duplicates that differs from the index of the other Series, or does not have the same length as the other input. Notes ----- The sign convention is the same for all the functions of this module. VaR is reported as a positive loss, so that a 99% VaR of 2.5 is the loss that is exceeded with probability ``p=0.01``, and an observation is an exception if :math:`-r_t > \mathrm{VaR}_t`. A quantile of the distribution of returns, which is negative for the lower tail, must be negated first. A loss that equals the VaR is not an exception. Only two Series are aligned on the index. A DataFrame, an array, or a Series used with an array, is matched by position, so the VaR forecast for the return in position :math:`t` must be in position :math:`t`. The forecasts of :meth:`~arch.univariate.base.ARCHModelResult.forecast` are indexed by the date of the forecast origin by default, so that the one-step forecast for day :math:`t` has the label of day :math:`t-1`. Use ``forecast(..., align="target")``, or shift the VaR forward by one observation, so that each VaR has the label of the return that it is a forecast of.

entries.name: arch.univariate.var_ratio
entries.summary: Ratio of Gaussian VaR to model-distribution VaR.
keywords: Ratio of Gaussian VaR to model-distribution VaR. Parameters ---------- p : float, optional The probability of an exception that the VaR is designed for, which is the size of the tail, in the open interval (0, 0.5). It is 0.05 for a 95% VaR and 0.01 for a 99% VaR. The default is 0.001, a 99.9% VaR. distribution : Distribution, optional Standardized distribution used to compute the model VaR. If not provided, uses the standard normal distribution. parameters : array_like, optional Distribution parameters. Must have one finite element for each parameter of ``distribution``. Use ``None`` for parameterless distributions. Returns ------- float Ratio of the Gaussian left-tail VaR to the VaR implied by the supplied model distribution. Raises ------ TypeError If ``p`` is not a real number, ``distribution`` is not a Distribution or ``parameters`` cannot be converted to numbers. ValueError If ``p`` is not in (0, 0.5), ``parameters`` does not have one finite element for each parameter of the distribution, or the model distribution does not produce a positive finite VaR. Notes ----- VaR is named by its confidence level, and ``p`` is the probability of an exception, as in the VaR backtests such as :func:`~arch.univariate.kupiec_pof`. The ratio is :math:`\Phi^{-1}(p)/F^{-1}(p)` where :math:`F` is the standardized distribution.

entries.name: arch.utility.array.append_same_type
entries.summary: Append observations to existing data, preserving the type of the data.
keywords: Append observations to existing data, preserving the type of the data. Parameters ---------- original : ndarray, Series, DataFrame, list or tuple The existing data. new : ndarray, Series, DataFrame, list, tuple or float The data to append. This must have the same type as original, unless original is an ndarray, list or tuple, in which case a scalar can be appended as a single observation. 1-d data appended to a 2-d ndarray with more than one column is treated as a single observation. sequence : bool, optional If True, ndarray, list and tuple data are a single sequence of observations that can be stored in any layout that can be squeezed to 1 dimension, e.g., (n,), (n, 1) or (1, n), and the layout of original is preserved. If False, 2-d data are observations (rows) by variables (columns), and new must have the same number of columns as original. Returns ------- ndarray, Series, DataFrame, list or tuple The extended data. Has the same type as original. The inputs are never modified. Raises ------ TypeError If the types of original and new are not compatible. ValueError If new does not contain any observations, has a different number of columns from original, or, when using a DataFrame, has different column labels. If sequence is True, also raised if original or new cannot be squeezed to 1 dimension.

entries.name: arch.utility.array.as_float64
entries.summary: Convert array_like data to a float64 ndarray.
keywords: Convert array_like data to a float64 ndarray. Parameters ---------- x : array_like The data. Integer, unsigned integer, Boolean, float32 and other real floating point data are converted to float64. Object data are converted if every element is a number, and are real if no element has an imaginary part different from 0, even if the elements are complex numbers. float16 data are not accepted. name : str The name of the variable. Used in error messages. allow_complex : bool, optional If True, complex data (complex64, complex128 or object data with an element that has an imaginary part different from 0) are converted to complex128. Real data are still converted to float64. If False, complex data are not accepted. Returns ------- ndarray The data as float64, or as complex128 if allow_complex and the data are complex, with the shape of x. This is x if x is an ndarray with dtype float64 or, if allow_complex, complex128. Raises ------ TypeError If the data cannot be converted to float64 (or complex128 if allow_complex), e.g., if the data are None or contain None, strings, dates or objects that are not numbers, or if they are float16, or complex unless allow_complex. Notes ----- NumPy converts None to NaN when it converts an object array, so that ``np.asarray(None).astype(float)`` is NaN. None is rejected here, as a value and as an element of an object array, so that a missing argument or value is not turned into a NaN. float32 data are converted to float64 and the calculations of the estimators are done in float64, so that their results do not depend on whether the data were stored in 32 or 64 bits. float16 data are rejected, since its 11 bits of precision (about 3 decimal digits) are not enough for any estimator; convert it with ``astype(np.float32)`` or ``astype(np.float64)`` if that is intended.

entries.name: arch.utility.array.cutoff_to_index
entries.summary: Convert a cutoff to a numerical index.
keywords: Convert a cutoff to a numerical index. Parameters ---------- cutoff : int, str, date, datetime, datetime64, Timestamp, Period or None The cutoff point to use. An int is the location of the observation, and must be between -len(index) and len(index), inclusive. A negative int counts from the end, as in Python slicing, so that -1 is len(index) - 1 and the result is never negative. Dates, strings and periods can only be used when index is a DatetimeIndex or a PeriodIndex, and must not be before the first or after the last date in index. A Period is converted to the first instant in the period. index : Index Pandas index. Must be a DatetimeIndex or a PeriodIndex if cutoff is a date, a datetime, a datetime64, a Timestamp, a Period or a string. default : int The value to return if cutoff is None. Must be between 0 and the length of index, inclusive. Returns ------- int The integer location of the cutoff, which is not negative. Raises ------ TypeError If cutoff is not None, an integer or a date-like value, index is not an Index, or default is not an integer. ValueError If default is an integer that is not between 0 and the length of index, cutoff is an integer that is not between -len(index) and len(index), or cutoff is a date-like value and the index is not a DatetimeIndex or a PeriodIndex, or the date is not within the index.

entries.name: arch.utility.array.date_to_index
entries.summary: Look up a date in an array of dates.
keywords: Look up a date in an array of dates. Parameters ---------- date : str, datetime, datetime64 or Timestamp Date to use when returning the index. date_index : DatetimeIndex, Series or ndarray Index data containing datetime64 values. Returns ------- int Index location. Raises ------ TypeError If date is not a str, a datetime, a datetime64 or a Timestamp, or date_index does not contain datetime64 values. ValueError If date_index is empty, is not increasing and unique, or date is a str that cannot be parsed to a date. Notes ----- Assumes dates are increasing and unique. The result is the location of date if it is in date_index, and otherwise the location where it would be inserted: 0 for a date before the first date and the length of date_index for a date after the last date. `cutoff_to_index` rejects the dates that are not within the index.

entries.name: arch.utility.array.ensure1d
entries.summary: Convert data to a 1-d float64 ndarray or Series.
keywords: Convert data to a 1-d float64 ndarray or Series. Parameters ---------- x : array_like, Series or DataFrame The data to convert. A DataFrame must have a single column, and any other input must have at most one dimension with more than one element. Integer, unsigned integer, Boolean and float32 data are converted to float64. float16 data are not accepted. name : Hashable or None The name of the variable. Used in error messages and as the name of the Series if x is not a Series or a DataFrame and series is True. series : bool, optional If True, return a Series. If False, return an ndarray. allow_complex : bool, optional If True, complex data are converted to complex128 and real data to float64. If False, complex data are not accepted. Returns ------- ndarray or Series The 1-d data. A Series if series is True and an ndarray otherwise. The dtype is float64, or complex128 if allow_complex and x is complex. The index of a Series is kept. x is returned, or is a view of x, if x is float64 data (or complex128 data if allow_complex). The name of a Series that is not a str is converted to a str. Raises ------ ValueError If x cannot be squeezed to 1 dimension. TypeError If x cannot be converted to real float64 values (None cannot be converted), or to complex128 values if allow_complex, if x is float16 or complex data that are not allowed, name is not hashable or series is not a bool. Notes ----- x is never modified. NaN and inf are not checked, because the function is used by code that handles them; the callers that need finite data check it.

entries.name: arch.utility.array.ensure2d
entries.summary: Convert data to a 2-d float64 DataFrame or ndarray.
keywords: Convert data to a 2-d float64 DataFrame or ndarray. Parameters ---------- x : array_like, Series or DataFrame The data to convert. A Series is converted to a DataFrame with a single column. A scalar is converted to an array with a single row and column, and a 1-d array_like to an array with a single column. Integer, unsigned integer, Boolean and float32 data are converted to float64. float16 data are not accepted. name : str The name of the variable. Used in error messages. allow_complex : bool, optional If True, complex data are converted to complex128 and real data to float64. If False, complex data are not accepted. Returns ------- DataFrame or ndarray The 2-d data with dtype float64, or complex128 if allow_complex and x is complex. A DataFrame if x is a Series or a DataFrame and an ndarray otherwise. The index and the column labels are kept. x is returned if it is a DataFrame or an ndarray with float64 data (or complex128 data if allow_complex). Raises ------ ValueError If x has more than 2 dimensions. TypeError If x cannot be converted to real float64 values (None cannot be converted), or to complex128 values if allow_complex, if x is float16 or complex data that are not allowed, or name is not a str. Notes ----- x is never modified. NaN and inf are not checked, because the function is used by code that handles them; the callers that need finite data check it.

A negative location counts from the end, as in Python indexing, so that -1 is nobs - 1. A non-negative location is returned unchanged. Returns ------- int Integer location of index value, which is not negative. Raises ------ TypeError If s is not a Series or a DataFrame, or index is not an integer, a str or a date-like value. entries.name: arch.utility.cov.check_array
entries.summary: Convert array_like data to float64 and check its dimensions and values.
keywords: Convert array_like data to float64 and check its dimensions and values. This uses the conversion of `arch.utility.array.as_float64`, which ``ensure1d`` and ``ensure2d`` also use. The result is an ndarray. Call ``ensure1d`` or ``ensure2d`` first if the index of a pandas object must be kept, and use this function for the checks. Parameters ---------- name : str The name of the argument, which is used in the error message. value : array_like, Series or DataFrame The data. Integer, unsigned integer, Boolean and float32 data are converted to float64. float16 data are not accepted. ndim : int, optional The number of dimensions of the result, 1 or 2. If ``squeeze`` is True, 1-d data can have any shape with a single dimension longer than 1 (a column, a row or a scalar) and 2-d data can be a scalar or 1-d (which becomes a column), as in ``ensure1d`` and ``ensure2d``. shape : sequence of int or None, optional The required shape of the result. None in a position accepts any size. The length of the sequence is the number of dimensions, and it replaces ``ndim``. min_length : int, optional The smallest accepted size of the first dimension. squeeze : bool, optional If False, ``ndim`` (or ``len(shape)``) must be the number of dimensions of the data exactly, and nothing is reshaped. allow_nan : bool, optional If True, NaN is accepted. allow_inf : bool, optional If True, inf and -inf are accepted. allow_none : bool, optional If True, None is accepted and returned unchanged. allow_complex : bool, optional If True, complex data are converted to complex128, and real data to float64. If False, complex data are not accepted. NaN and inf are checked in the real and the imaginary part. Returns ------- ndarray or None The float64 data, or the complex128 data if ``allow_complex`` and the data are complex. This is ``value`` itself if it is a float64 ndarray (or complex128 if ``allow_complex``) with the required number of dimensions. None if ``allow_none`` and ``value`` is None. Raises ------ TypeError If the data cannot be converted to float64 (strings, dates, objects that are not numbers, None), are float16, or are complex numbers and ``allow_complex`` is False. ValueError If the data do not have the required number of dimensions, shape or length, or contain NaN or inf where that is not allowed.

keywords: Check a flag. Parameters ---------- name : str The name of the argument, which is used in the error message. value : object The value passed by the user. ``bool``, ``np.bool_`` and the integers 0 and 1 (Python ``int`` and NumPy integers) are accepted. Other integers, floats (including 1.0), strings and arrays are rejected. allow_none : bool, optional If True, None is accepted and returned unchanged. Use this only where None is the documented default. Returns ------- bool or None The flag as a Python bool, or None if ``allow_none`` and ``value`` is None. Raises ------ TypeError If the value is not a bool or an integer (or None if ``allow_none``). ValueError If the value is an integer other than 0 and 1.

entries.name: arch.utility.cov.check_int
entries.summary: Check an integer.
keywords: Check an integer. Parameters ---------- name : str The name of the argument, which is used in the error message. value : object The value passed by the user. Python and NumPy integers are accepted, using ``operator.index``. Floats, including 5.0, and Booleans are rejected. lower : int, optional The smallest accepted value (inclusive). upper : int, optional The largest accepted value (inclusive). allow_none : bool, optional If True, None is accepted and returned unchanged. Returns ------- int or None The value as a Python int, or None if ``allow_none`` and ``value`` is None. Raises ------ TypeError If the value is not an integer (or None if ``allow_none``). ValueError If the value is smaller than ``lower`` or larger than ``upper``.

entries.name: arch.utility.cov.cov_nw
entries.summary: Compute the Newey-West covariance for 1-d and 2-d arrays.
keywords: Compute the Newey-West covariance for 1-d and 2-d arrays. Parameters ---------- y : array_like Values to use when computing the Newey-West covariance estimator, either 1-d or 2-d. When y is 2d, default behavior is to treat columns as variables and rows as observations. Integer, Boolean and float32 data are converted to float64, and complex data to complex128. float16 data are not accepted. Must not contain NaN or infinite values. lags : int, optional Number of lags to include in the Newey-West covariance estimator. Must be non-negative and at most the number of observations. demean : bool, optional Indicates whether to subtract the mean. axis : int, optional The axis to use when y is 2d. ddof : int, optional Degree of freedom correction for compatibility with simple covariance estimators. Must be non-negative and smaller than the number of observations. Returns ------- float or ndarray The estimated covariance. A float if y is 1-d and a 2-d ndarray otherwise. The covariance of complex data is Hermitian, so that it is real if y is 1-d and a complex128 matrix if y is 2-d. Raises ------ TypeError If y cannot be converted to float64 or complex128 (it is float16, or contains strings or objects that are not numbers) or if lags, demean, axis or ddof have the wrong type. Booleans and floats are not accepted for the integers. ValueError If y is not 1-d or 2-d, is empty or contains NaN or infinite values, or if lags, axis or ddof are outside their range. Notes ----- The covariance of complex data is the Hermitian covariance, which uses the conjugate transpose: the term at lag j is the sum of z_t times the conjugate of z_{t-j}, and a term and its conjugate transpose are added for each lag. It is the covariance of the Bartlett kernel estimator in :mod:`arch.covariance.kernel`. The pseudo-covariance is not estimated.

entries.name: arch.utility.timeseries.add_trend
entries.summary: Add a trend and/or constant to an array.
keywords: Add a trend and/or constant to an array. Parameters ---------- x : array_like or DataFrame, optional Original array of data. If None, then nobs must be a positive integer. Integer, unsigned integer, Boolean and float32 data are converted to float64, and complex data to complex128. float16 data are not accepted. NaN and inf in x are not checked and are returned unchanged. trend : {"n", "c", "t", "ct", "ctt"}, optional The trend(s) to add. Not case sensitive. Supported options are: * "n" no trend (no-op) * "c" add constant only * "t" add trend only * "ct" add constant and linear trend * "ctt" add constant and linear and quadratic trend. prepend : bool, optional If True, prepends the new data to the columns of x. nobs : int, optional Positive integer containing the length of the trend series. Must be None if x is provided. has_constant : {"raise", "add", "skip"}, optional Controls what happens when trend is "c", "ct" or "ctt" and a constant already exists in x. "raise" will raise an error. "add" will duplicate a constant. "skip" will return the data without change. "skip" is the default. Not case sensitive. Returns ------- ndarray or DataFrame The trend if x is None, an ndarray with nobs rows. Otherwise x with the trend columns added, which is a DataFrame if x is a DataFrame and an ndarray otherwise. The trend columns of a DataFrame are named "const", "trend" and "quadratic_trend". The trend columns are real, and the data are complex128 if x is complex. Raises ------ TypeError If trend or has_constant is not a str, prepend is not a bool, nobs is not an integer, or x cannot be converted to float64 or complex128 data (it is float16, or contains strings or objects that are not numbers). ValueError If trend or has_constant is not one of the supported options, if both or neither of x and nobs are provided, if nobs is not positive, or if has_constant is "raise" and x already contains a constant. Notes ----- The columns of the trend are ordered constant, linear trend and quadratic trend whenever applicable. There is currently no checking for an existing trend.
